messages.subject: C-900 crusher problems - need legal advice
messages.plaintextBody:
Tom,

Good to speak just now. As discussed, the C-900 crushing plant we bought from Crayford last summer has been a disaster - bearing failures three times, hydraulics dropping out, and it has never once hit the 320 tonnes an hour they guaranteed. We've had a hired spread in since September just to keep the contracts going.

We want to know where we stand and to get money back. Karen Doust (my plant manager) has kept a full diary and all the weighbridge data. Can you take a look and tell us if we have a claim?

Owen Marsden
Managing Director, Marldale Aggregates Limited

messages.subject: RE: C-900 crusher problems - need legal advice
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Owen,

Thank you - it does sound as though you have a strong contractual claim for breach of the performance and parts warranties, and likely under the Sale of Goods Act as well. The key will be the throughput data and Karen's breakdown records.

I'll send our engagement letter today. In the meantime, please ask Karen not to alter or overwrite any of the PLC logs or the plant diary - those are exactly the documents we'll need.

I'm copying Sarah Whitfield, who is supervising.

Tom Gallagher
Associate | Litigation
Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
T +44 (0)20 7946 5500

Confidential and may be legally privileged.
